title: Hash-warmstart prober: temporal workload fingerprinting for adaptive kernel warm starts
creator: Aisha Kumar
description: Goal: reduce latency tail and token-cost by quickly selecting a near-optimal kernel implementation on a per-request temporal-workload basis. Approach: compute a compact hash-based fingerprint for each request (features: model architecture family, quantization profile, incoming sequence-length, recent per-client seqlen histogram, batch size, and time-of-day bucket). Use a short-lived warm-start cache mapping fingerprint -> kernel-config (microkernel variant, threads, vector-width policy) with metadata (last-tested latency, error margin, TTL). A lightweight epsilon-greedy prober runs at low probability per-fingerprint to explore alternatives and update cost estimates. The system decays scores over time and respects safety constraints (hard latency SLO floors per-customer, prefer conservative fallback when uncertainty high). Expected benefits: faster cold-start selection for new but repeated workload patterns (eg. same customer or route), fewer exploratory microbenchmarks in the realtime path, reduced tail latency for mixed prefills and decodes. Metrics: p50/p95/p99 latency, token-cost, probe budget utilization, misselection regret and rollback rate. Deliverables: design doc, simulator for offline evaluation, runtime instrumentation + dashboard, canary rollout to 5% of traffic with automatic rollback triggers.
comments: 2026-01-11 — Aisha Kumar: Initial triage completed. Spike validated that a fingerprint of ~64 bits (Bloom-style) captures sufficient seqlen+arch clustering on our production traces. Created design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RUNTIME/ENG-734512-hash-warmstart-prober

2026-01-18 — Markus Chen: Prototype of fingerprint generator merged to branch feat/eng-734512. Microbench harness added for three candidate kernels per model family. See PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4532

2026-01-22 — Performance lab: Offline simulation across 7 days of prod traces shows median probe budget 0.8% with 18% reduction in p99 for mixed-prefill routes; some high-variance routes saw no improvement. Uploaded results: https://dashboards.redwood.ai/d/runtime/eng-734512-sim

2026-01-25 — Design review notes (from PM & SRE): Prefer decoupling probe logic from hot execution path; suggestion to run probes as asynchronous background invocations to avoid inflating tail latency. Action: implement probe queue with backpressure and time-budget per-worker. Assigned to: Markus.

2026-01-29 — Security review (Chris Patel): no sensitive data in fingerprint, but flagged telemetry privacy — ensure hashed client identifiers and opt-out respect. Added privacy checklist to design doc.

2026-01-31 — Markus Chen: Implemented asynchronous probe queue + rate limiter. Local canary (10k reqs) shows no p99 regression and probe success updated mapping in ~130ms median. Pushed PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4689

2026-02-01 — QA (Lina Ortiz): Integration test failure flake observed when probe budget exhausted under bursty traffic — probe queue backpressure triggered rollback but mapping update race detected. Root cause: stale compare-and-swap on mapping update; mitigated by sequencing token. Created follow-up task ENG-734513 to address mapping CAS backoff.

2026-02-02 — Aisha Kumar: Planning canary rollout to 5% of non-SLA-critical Hosted API routes next week. Rollout plan includes thresholds: if p99 increases >5% for 5m or error rate increases >0.2% we will auto-revert. Also added observability endpoints and Grafana dashboard panels for probe budget and misselection incidents. Next steps: finish CAS fix, add per-customer opt-out, and schedule A/B experiment with Dedicated fleets.
